title: Consolidate the eleven NFL desks into one index
problem: Eleven sessions have answered this brief in eleven namespaces. A reader cannot tell which page is current, and four desks publish different counts for the same requirement.
options: A. Leave them; they are independent evidence. | B. One index page that names, for each requirement, the desk that owns it. | C. Retire the duplicates and keep one.
recommendation: B. An index costs one page and destroys nothing; C deletes another session's work.
what_would_change_the_call: If the desks are found to disagree on a fact rather than on a definition, C becomes the right answer.

title: Buy or license an opening-line history
problem: Without an open there is no CLV and no 'fade the move'. This is the single largest constraint on the project.
options: A. Use only closing lines and drop all move-based strategies permanently. | B. License a two-snapshot history (open and close) for one book. | C. Capture our own two snapshots from now on and wait.
recommendation: C as a start (free, honest, slow), with B priced in parallel. A is a legitimate fallback: the desk already shows the market is hard to beat.
what_would_change_the_call: If three months of self-captured opens show no residual alpha, B is not worth buying.

title: Publish a two-series comparison for every backtest
problem: The two price series disagree on 23% of joinable games. A single-series backtest hides that sensitivity.
options: A. Publish one series only. | B. Publish every ROI twice, once per series, with the gap. | C. Publish the gap only where it changes the sign of the ROI.
recommendation: B until the provenance question (Q-02) is settled, then C.
what_would_change_the_call: If every strategy keeps its sign under both series, C is enough.

title: Adopt the nflverse pinned commit as the corpus of record
problem: The corpus is currently re-downloaded; a moving HEAD would silently change every number.
options: A. Pin a commit and publish its hash (done here). | B. Track master and rebuild nightly. | C. Vendor the whole repository.
recommendation: A, with the pin re-proved on every build. C if the repository disappears.
what_would_change_the_call: If the pinned commit stops being served, move to C.

title: Add a second clock time for every availability unit
problem: Five of six units have exactly one clock time, so no replay test is possible for them.
options: A. Capture daily at a fixed hour. | B. Capture on the league's own cadence (Wed/Thu/Fri). | C. Capture only before each kickoff.
recommendation: B for the injury report and A for depth, transactions and reserve list.
what_would_change_the_call: If the Week 11 report publishes before the next capture, the delta table stays empty and the cadence question is moot for this week.

title: Publish the model's inputs as a downloadable row-level file
problem: The site is a public analysis layer by policy, so the raw rows are not published. That also makes the model unauditable from the site alone.
options: A. Publish derived tables only (current). | B. Publish a hash of the input file and a reproducible script. | C. Publish the inputs.
recommendation: B: the script and the hash are in the repository, so a reader can rebuild without the site carrying row-level data.
what_would_change_the_call: If the terms of the data source forbid even derived redistribution, fall back to A.

title: Set the reward structure before the first certified strategy
problem: A reward pool defined after a winner appears can always be tuned to that winner.
options: A. Cash prizes. | B. Non-cash badges and a public record. | C. Nothing until a strategy is certified.
recommendation: B now, with the rule text frozen, and revisit A only after a certified strategy exists.
what_would_change_the_call: If no strategy is ever certified, the reward question is moot and no money is at risk.

title: Replace the ridge penalty with a hierarchical prior
problem: The team ratings use a single ridge constant, which is a modelling choice and a flag. A hierarchical model would shrink early-season ratings by observed rather than assumed variance.
options: A. Keep ridge (current). | B. Empirical Bayes on the ridge constant by week. | C. Full hierarchical fit.
recommendation: B: it is a small change, it is measurable on the holdout, and it removes a hand-set constant.
what_would_change_the_call: If B does not improve holdout Brier skill against the close, keep A.

title: Publish a proper-score tournament instead of a leaderboard
problem: A leaderboard is a ranking; a tournament is a rule with a winner. With zero certified strategies there is nothing to rank.
options: A. Keep an empty leaderboard. | B. Publish the bootstrap distribution of Brier skill so a reader sees the uncertainty, not just a rank. | C. Delay all ranking until a strategy is certified.
recommendation: B now and C as the permanent rule: nothing is ranked until it is certified.
what_would_change_the_call: If a strategy clears all nine gates, the tournament question becomes live and must be frozen before its first live bet.

title: Treat the 7,088-game corpus as a baseline, not a result
problem: A long backtest feels like evidence. It is a description of the past unless the rule survived an out-of-sample split.
options: A. Report in-sample and holdout side by side (current). | B. Report holdout only. | C. Report the full sample with a deflated statistic.
recommendation: A plus C: the holdout is the answer and the full sample is the context.
what_would_change_the_call: If A and C disagree on the sign, the rule is not robust and the answer is no.

title: Add a manual review queue to the flags page
problem: Flags are published but there is no way for the owner to accept or reject one in the repository.
options: A. Keep the flags static. | B. One row per flag with a decision column the owner fills in. | C. A GitHub issue per flag.
recommendation: C: it is native to the repository, it is auditable, and it needs no build step.
what_would_change_the_call: If the owner never opens issues, B is lower friction.

title: Publish a season-to-date error track for the model
problem: A single holdout number hides whether the model is improving.
options: A. Publish the holdout number only. | B. Publish MAE by week for 2026. | C. Publish a rolling 4-week MAE.
recommendation: B: 149 finals are enough to see the shape, and it costs one table.
what_would_change_the_call: If the by-week MAE is dominated by blowouts, add C to smooth it.

title: Raise the corpus to include player game logs
problem: Two of the brief's market types (player props and same-game parlays) cannot be priced at all without player-level results.
options: A. Leave them blocked. | B. Add a play-by-play corpus and derive player lines. | C. Buy a player-stats feed.
recommendation: B if the host becomes reachable; C otherwise.
what_would_change_the_call: If B's derived totals cannot reproduce an official box score, B is not good enough and C is required.

title: Make the price policy visible on every number
problem: A reader can quote an ROI without knowing the policy it was computed under.
options: A. A note in the methodology. | B. A policy badge in every table header. | C. A policy column on every row.
recommendation: B: one badge, repeated, is enough.
what_would_change_the_call: If readers still misquote, move to C.

title: Schedule the build, not just the capture
problem: This desk is rebuilt when a session runs. A monthly rebuild would make every freshness number stale and every delta empty.
options: A. Rebuild on demand. | B. A nightly workflow that rebuilds and fails on drift. | C. A weekly manual rebuild.
recommendation: B, mirroring the pattern this repository already uses for its other desks.
what_would_change_the_call: If a nightly rebuild is too noisy because the corpus moves, pin the corpus and rebuild only the captures.

title: Decide what a certified strategy would actually be allowed to do
problem: The gates say what skill must be shown. They do not say what happens next.
options: A. Nothing: certification is a label. | B. A staking plan with a hard cap, decided in advance. | C. A public pick record with no money.
recommendation: C until the owner chooses B in writing. The gates are a filter, not a licence.
what_would_change_the_call: If the owner's jurisdiction forbids even a public pick record, A is the answer.
